name: Even Subarrays
description: You are given an integer array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). Find the number of subarrays of $$$a$$$ whose $$$\operatorname{XOR}$$$ has an even number of divisors. In other words, find all pairs of indices $$$(i, j)$$$ ($$$i \le j$$$) such that $$$a_i \oplus a_{i + 1} \oplus \dots \oplus a_j$$$ has an even number of divisors. For example, numbers $$$2$$$, $$$3$$$, $$$5$$$ or $$$6$$$ have an even number of divisors, while $$$1$$$ and $$$4$$$ — odd. Consider that $$$0$$$ has an odd number of divisors in this task. Here $$$\operatorname{XOR}$$$ (or $$$\oplus$$$) denotes the bitwise XOR operation . Print the number of subarrays but multiplied by 2022... Okay, let's stop. Just print the actual answer.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$). Description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq n$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the number of subarrays, whose $$$\operatorname{XOR}$$$ has an even number of divisors.
approach_summary: Compute polynomial rolling hashes hash(s[0..i]) with prime base B and large modulo M. Check substring equality s[l1..r1] == s[l2..r2] in O(1) time.
